context: The user has a normal token and a stepped-up token that are technically the same token type but gate different endpoints, and integrators are confused. The criteria check whether the answer models security schemes as discrete named contracts, separates the credential's implementation from the consumer-facing scheme, and treats normal vs stepped-up as functionally different schemes.

checklist.name: Schemes as discrete named contracts
checklist.description: Treats security schemes as discrete, named contracts rather than one vague 'API key' instruction

checklist.name: Endpoint maps to one scheme
checklist.description: Each endpoint maps to exactly one named scheme that it declares

checklist.name: Separates credential from scheme
checklist.description: Separates the credential's implementation (e.g. an API key) from the consumer-facing scheme — makes the API-key-to-header transform explicit

checklist.name: Normal vs stepped-up are different schemes
checklist.description: Explains that the normal and stepped-up tokens are functionally different schemes even though technically the same token type

checklist.name: Each endpoint declares requirement
checklist.description: Each endpoint declares which scheme (normal vs stepped-up) it requires

checklist.name: Recommends explicit modelling
checklist.description: Recommends modelling this explicitly, e.g. OpenAPI named `securitySchemes` plus per-operation `security`
